**Group:** Dinoflagellates  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A desmokont dinoflagellate whose theca is made of two large valves joined along a lengthwise suture, like a clam shell or shield, with __no__ cingulum or sulcus grooves. The two flagella emerge together from an apical area that often bears a small tooth or spine. Cells are oval, heart-, or teardrop-shaped in valve view. Species in Monterey Bay may be narrow (_P. gracile_) or wide (_P. micans_ etc). Key features: two-valve clam-like theca, apical tooth, absence of a girdle.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **dinophysis** | Dinophysis is also two-parted but bears a funnel cingular list and sail-like sulcal lists; Prorocentrum is a plain two-valved cell with an apical spine and no lists. |
| **ceratium** | Ceratium has long horns and an obvious girdle; Prorocentrum has neither. |
| **gyrodinium** | Gyrodinium has a distinct girdle groove that wraps aroudn teh cell. From girdle view, both can have a similar shape. |
